div.head: VI Atr 5.2
div.ab: Ac hit is þe wyrse, þe sume habbað twa oððe ma, ⁊ sum, þeh he forlæte þa he ær hæfde, he be lifiendre þære eft oþere nimð, swa ænigan Cristenan mæn ne gedafenað to donne.
Ac hit is þe wyrse þe sume habbað twa oððe ma, ⁊ sum, þeh he forlæte þa he ær hæfde, he be lifiendre þære eft oþere nimð, swa ænigan Cristenan man ne gedafenað to donne.
Ac hit is þe wyrse þe sume habbað twa oððe ma, and sum—þeh he forlæte þa he ær hæfde—he be lifiendre þære eft oþere nimð, swa ænigan Cristenan mæn ne gedafenað to donne.

Aber es ist um so schlimmer, dass einige zwei oder mehr [Weiber] haben, und mancher, obschon er die, welche er früher gehabt hatte, verlässt [-liess?], bei deren Lebzeiten nachher eine andere [Frau] nimmt, wie keinem Christenmenschen zu thun ziemt.

But it is all the worse that some have two or more [women], and some, although they abandon the one they had before, afterwards take another [woman] while the first is still living, as befits no Christian man to do.

But some are guilty of a worse practice in having two or more [wives], and others, although they forsake their former wives, afterwards take others while these are still alive—a thing which is unfitting for any Christian man to do.
But it is the worse in that some have two or more, and some—though they abandon those they had before—then take others while these are yet living, which it does not behoove any Christian man to do.

note.label: expanded in
note.quote: VI Ethelred 5.2 adds that some have two wives or more, and some desert one and take another.

note.seg: Dieser Satz, als deutlich den Zusammenhang von 5, 1 und 5, 3 unterbrechend, scheint ein privater Nachtrag des Schreibers, vielleicht, da L und D fehlend, nur durch K; s. o. Einl. 21. Doch lag der Satz vielleicht Northu 35 bereits vor. Auch den Laien wird Vielweiberei verboten (u. 12, 3) und zweite Ehe, solange der andere Teil lebt, verpönt; s. Gl Ehebruch 3ff.; Ehe 5; Geistliche 29b ff.

This sentence, since it clearly interrupts the connexion between 5, 1 and 5, 3, seems to be a private addition by the scribe, perhaps, since L and D lack it, made only by K; see above Introduction 21. However, the sentence was perhaps already available to Northu 35. Polygamy is forbidden to laymen too (below 12, 3), and a second marriage while the other partner is still living is condemned; see Gl Ehebruch 3ff.; Ehe 5; Geistliche 29b ff.
Das Präteritum liegt nur vor, falls æ statt e steht, was vorkommt; s. Wb: æ 3. So schreibt læton für Präteritum leton II Cn 76, 2 B
The preterite is present only if æ stands for e, which does occur; see Wb: æ 3. Thus læton is written for the preterite leton II Cn 76, 2 B
Cf. 12, 1; N.P.L. 35. Liebermann suggests that this clause, which is not found in V Atr. or in the Latin paraphrase, is an addition of the scribe’s.
